scope: Minnesota DHS 14 high-risk Medicaid service/provider categories
evidence_rule: A DHS high-risk designation describes programmatic vulnerability, suspicious patterns, evidence of fraudulent activity, or claim anomalies. It is not a finding that every provider, recipient, or payment in the category is fraudulent.

common_controls.enrollment_moratoria: As of July 2026, 12 of 14 high-risk services have a CMS-approved enrollment moratorium through 2027-01-27; EIDBI has a separate moratorium through 2026-10-31; HSS ended 2025-10-31.

services.name: Adult Companion Services
services.purpose: Non-medical care, supervision and socialization that helps an older adult work toward a therapeutic or community-integration goal in the support plan.

case_coverage.summary: Direct allegation coverage exists, but no current case in the corpus isolates an Adult Companion-only loss figure.

cases.case: State v. Mohamed Abdirashid Omarxeyd / Guardian Home Health Services
cases.role: Companion care is one of several HCBS services in the alleged Guardian scheme.
AG alleges more than 6,000 hours across PCA, companion care and homemaker services; >$125,000 mixed-service alleged loss.

services.money_status: No service-only charged/proven-loss figure isolated in current corpus.
open_gaps: Acquire Jackson complaint for service-by-service claim counts and amounts.
Do not allocate Guardian's broader >$3.2M alleged scheme total to companion care.

services.name: Adult Day Services
services.purpose: Individualized daytime activities, supervision, care, assistance and training designed around an older adult's assessed health and social needs.
legal_or_program_authority: Federally approved BI, CADI, DD and EW waiver plans

case_coverage.summary: No dedicated Minnesota Medicaid-billing prosecution for Adult Day Services was located in the current corpus/search pass.

adjacent_records.record: 2019 federal tax prosecution involving owners of Meisa Group, an adult day care serving Medicaid recipients
adjacent_records.qualification: Tax evasion/conspiracy allegations based on personal use of company income; not evidence that adult-day Medicaid claims themselves were fraudulent.

current_controls: High-risk enhanced screening and pre-payment review
Adult-day licensing/enrollment controls and statewide high-risk moratorium framework
open_gaps: Search MFCU historical complaints and civil recoveries for adult-day billing cases.
Acquire provider-count and annual-spend series before drawing growth conclusions.

services.name: Adult Rehabilitative Mental Health Services
services.purpose: Rehabilitative mental-health services intended to build psychiatric stability, social competencies, personal and emotional adjustment, and independent living/community skills impaired by mental illness.

cases.case: State v. Salman Ahmed Elmi / Reva Health
cases.summary: Eight felony theft charges; AG alleges false documentation, kickbacks, ineligible providers and inadequate supervision.

services.money_status: Reva >$1M is a dedicated charged allegation; Wavra amount is mixed-service. Neither is adjudicated loss as of captured sources.
open_gaps: Acquire Reva and Wavra complaints for count-level extraction.
Capture official annual provider/spend series rather than journalism-derived growth figures.

services.name: Assertive Community Treatment
services.purpose: Intensive nonresidential, team-based rehabilitative mental-health treatment providing a single point of responsibility for treatment, rehabilitation and support, with services available 24/7 in community settings.

case_coverage.summary: No Minnesota ACT-specific fraud prosecution was located in the current research corpus/search pass. This is not evidence that fraud is absent.

current_controls: High-risk enhanced screening and pre-payment review

DHS Behavioral Health Administration engaged Health Management Associates in 2026 to review ACT, IRTS and Residential Crisis Services payment policies/rate methodology, including program-integrity objectives.
open_gaps: Acquire ACT provider count, annual claims/spend, and HMA review deliverables when issued.
Search historical MFCU and civil False Claims Act records for ACT-specific matters.

services.name: Community First Services and Supports
services.purpose: Flexible assistance for people with disabilities and other health needs to support independence in their homes and communities; replaced PCA and the Consumer Support Grant beginning 2024-10-01.

case_coverage.summary: No CFSS-specific fraud prosecution was located. Numerous PCA prosecutions exist, but they predate or involve the predecessor PCA service and must not be relabeled as CFSS fraud.

current_controls: Transition from extended PCA continues; DHS says extended PCA ends 2026-09-30 while regular PCA can continue until an individual completes transition to CFSS.
open_gaps: Track PCA-to-CFSS claims migration so legacy PCA fraud data are not mixed with CFSS.
Acquire CFSS provider/spend data after transition stabilizes.

services.name: Early Intensive Developmental and Behavioral Intervention
services.purpose: Medically necessary services and supports for people under age 21 with autism spectrum disorder or related conditions, intended to support development, independence and participation in family, school and community life.

cases.status: CHARGED in captured primary source; later plea requires primary docket/USAO confirmation

cases.case: Smart Therapy + Star Autism / Shamso Ahmed Hassan and Hanaan Mursal Yusuf
cases.qualification: Overlaps the earlier provider-specific $14M and $6M figures; do not sum.

current_controls: DHS reported an Aug. 2026 authorization backlog caused by increased review volume
services.money_status: Multiple overlapping charged/paid figures exist; no single additive EIDBI fraud total is valid from captured sources.
open_gaps: Normalize all EIDBI charging instruments and judgments.
Capture annual provider count and program spend from primary DHS/CMS data.
Quantify authorization backlog only if DHS publishes counts.

services.name: Housing Stabilization Services
services.purpose: A state-plan HCBS Medical Assistance benefit created to help people with disabilities and seniors find and keep housing in their own homes.
services.program_status: Ended at 11:59 p.m. on 2025-10-31; no HSS services after that date are reimbursable.

case_coverage.summary: Multiple federal HSS charge waves cover Brilliant Minds, Faladcare, Leo Human Services, Liberty Plus, Pristine Health, SafeLodgings, House of Heroes, Cradle of Love, North/South Home Health, Cynthia Allen Servicing, Candice Carene, Vitality and others.
case_coverage.current_adjudication: All four Brilliant Minds defendants pleaded guilty in July 2026; Anwar and Asad Adow also have captured guilty-plea docket facts.

services.money_status: Program spend and case amounts are separately typed; billed/paid amounts across HSS cases are not one loss total.
open_gaps: Acquire Brilliant Minds plea agreements/judgments and HSS sentencing records.
Reconcile HSS historical launch/spend vintages across government sources without silently overwriting them.

services.name: Individualized Home Supports
services.purpose: Support and/or training in community-living service categories for people who live in their own home or family home, with service variants based on needed support/training.
legal_or_program_authority: Federally approved BI, CAC, CADI and DD waiver plans

cases.case: Healey Homes / Charles Wayne Healey and Katherin Suzan Larsen-Guthmiller
cases.summary: Government alleges IHS was billed in provider-controlled residences despite the own-home program requirement.
Mixed HCBS complaint includes IHS and alleged ineligible sleep-hour billing, including >$45,000 in one described IHS example.

services.money_status: Healey Homes is a dedicated charged case figure; Guardian figures are mixed/examples and must not be added as a separate IHS-wide loss.
open_gaps: Acquire Healey charging instrument and later docket outcomes for count-level normalization.
Build provider-controlled-setting vs own-home rule explainer from controlling waiver/statutory text.

services.name: Integrated Community Supports
services.purpose: Support and training/habilitation in community-living categories for adults living in provider-controlled ICS settings; services may be delivered up to 24 hours a day in the person's living unit or community.
legal_or_program_authority: BI and CADI waiver plans from 2021
CAC and DD waiver plans from 2023

cases.case: Ultimate Home Health Services / Ahmed Othman Kadar
cases.amount: about $1.4M billed/paid in May 2026 indictment description
cases.summary: Government alleges billing for high-hour ICS services not provided.

services.money_status: Government program-spend descriptions of >$400M and later >$460M since 2021 are program spend, not fraud loss.
open_gaps: Acquire indictment and exact count/transaction table if not already normalized.
Build annual spend/provider/site count series from primary state data.

services.name: Intensive Residential Treatment Services
services.purpose: Time-limited, community-based, medically monitored residential mental-health treatment for adults, with qualified mental-health staff on site 24 hours a day and a goal of psychiatric stability and transition to a more independent setting.

case_coverage.summary: No Minnesota IRTS-specific fraud prosecution was located in the current corpus/search pass.

current_controls: 2026 DHS/HMA review of payment policies and rate methodology for IRTS, ACT and Residential Crisis Services, framed in part around strengthening program integrity
open_gaps: Acquire HMA deliverables when published.
Capture provider count, bed/capacity, annual spend and any MFCU referrals.

services.name: Night Supervision Services
services.purpose: Overnight assistance and supervision in a person's own home when an assessed need exists for specified support, ADL/IADL or skill-development activities; the service cannot be used as merely preventative or assumptive safety monitoring.
legal_or_program_authority: Federally approved BI, CAC, CADI and DD waiver plans

cases.summary: Complaint discusses companion-care night-supervision billing and alleges ineligible sleeping/overnight claims; no standalone Night Supervision scheme total is stated.

services.current_program_change: Beginning in 2026 DHS separates awake and asleep night-supervision rate frameworks under the Disability Waiver Rate System.
services.money_status: No standalone service-wide charged loss figure located.
open_gaps: Extract Guardian count-level night-supervision transactions from complaint/claims exhibits if available.
Avoid treating all overnight IHS or companion-care billing as the Night Supervision service.

services.name: Nonemergency Medical Transportation Services
services.purpose: Transportation enabling Medical Assistance members to travel to and from covered nonemergency medical appointments using the safest, appropriate and cost-effective mode.

cases.case: Driving Miss Daisy / Charles Omato and LaTonia Jackson
cases.summary: AG alleges rides not provided and impossible travel-time claims.

current_controls: Seven-county metro new-provider enrollment moratorium extended through 2027-01-27
DHS announced 2026 NEMT provider-claim compliance reviews with Myers & Stauffer on 2026-08-24
services.money_status: > $1.4M is a charged allegation, not adjudicated loss or restitution.
open_gaps: Acquire Omato/Jackson complaint and current case disposition.
Capture results of 2026 Myers & Stauffer reviews when published.

services.name: Recovery Peer Support
services.purpose: Peer-delivered substance-use-disorder recovery support, including individualized peer support and recovery planning intended to advance recovery goals, self-sufficiency, self-advocacy and natural supports.

case_coverage.summary: No Minnesota Recovery Peer Support-specific criminal fraud case was located in the current corpus/search pass.

current_controls: 2026 law includes service restrictions/billing limits; current statute makes noncompliant peer-recovery payments subject to monetary recovery
open_gaps: Acquire annual provider/client/spend series.
Track monetary-recovery actions separately from criminal fraud cases.

services.name: Recuperative Care
services.purpose: Short-term medical care and support for eligible people experiencing homelessness who do not need hospital-level care but cannot safely recover from physical illness in a shelter or while unhoused.

case_coverage.summary: No Minnesota Recuperative Care-specific fraud prosecution was located in the current corpus/search pass.

current_controls: Pre-enrollment risk assessment and habitability inspection requirements
Prior authorization required for all recuperative-care services effective 2026-08-01
open_gaps: Capture annual spend/provider/facility counts since 2024 launch.
Evaluate whether prior-authorization changes produce measurable denial/recovery results without equating denials with fraud.

cross_cutting_gaps: Create annual spend and provider-count series for all 14 categories from a common primary dataset and fixed time window.
Normalize every known criminal case to complaint/indictment, plea/verdict, judgment, restitution, forfeiture and appeal.
Track administrative payment holds, disenrollment, sanctions, identified-for-recovery and actual collections as separate event types.
For categories with no dedicated case located, continue historical MFCU/FCA searches; absence from this pass is not evidence of absence.
Do not aggregate the 14 categories into a total fraud figure.
